free_tier.stated: [translated] 'One Micro Server can be created per person. Free use for one year from the moment payment information is registered. A Micro Server not returned when the free period ends is billed automatically. However, this is provided only when the country of residence is Korea.'

egress.terms: [translated] One year of a Micro Server, one per person. No traffic allowance is stated for it on the page. The separate new-signup credit is '100,000 won of discount credit, valid for 3 months'.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: [translated] The console creates the server; the platform documents an API and CLI for its services.
tooling: console and API (the platform ships an OpenAPI and CLI); WireGuard would run in the guest
chaining: Unreachable, so it chains with nothing.
binding_note: The account is refused before any quota is reached: a Korean residence is the first constraint and no byte allowance matters behind it.

identity_cost.detail: [translated] 'However, this is provided only when the country of residence is Korea.' The page adds: 'If you register payment information after signing up, you can create a Micro Server', so a payment method is a second gate behind the residence one. The 200,000 won Green Rookie credit goes further and requires an email at a partner Korean school or university.

reliability_note: The free server is billed automatically if not returned at the end of the year; the discount credit expires after three months and cannot be applied to products that already have a free period.
confidence_note: The residence restriction is a vendor sentence on the credit-event page read on 2026-10-23. What would change the verdict is a Korean residence, which the client does not have; nothing measurable on the network side would.
